title: Telling: anecdotes, unexpected and reported speech

blocks.text: With Layer B2 The Egyptian track passes from the phrases of everyday life to long conversation. The first step is the story: in Egypt, telling is an art, and a well-told story (ḥikāya) has a precise rhythm, with an attack, suspense, surprise, and a listener who reacts to every joke. In this unit learn the signs of the story (fi l-awwil, wi fagʾa, the-muhimm), the times of the past that serve to tell (kunt ba-..., kunt ḥa-..., kunt lissa...), the listener's reactions (lā yā šēḫ!, ya ḫabar!) and the speech reported in Egyptian: what he said, what he asked, what he said to do. Nine weeks, in parallel with B2-01, B2-02 and B2-03.

rows: 12–13 9 weeks (weeks) 157–165), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian conversation partner, video or story podcast in Egyptian (Appendix C)
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. tell Egyptian an episode of 2–3 minutes with a clear order and a little suspense;
2. use the time of the story: past, progressive past (kunt ba-), ḥa-), I had
a.
3. react to a story like an Egyptian listener;
4. report what someone has said, asked or ordered (ʾāl inn... saʾal Law... ʾalli aʿmil…);
5. follow an authentic recorded tale and summarize it.
Nine-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).

⁧الله يسلمك. اسمع يا سيدي،⁩ : ⁧ياسمين⁩ ⁧الرحلة نفسها كانت حلوة، بس اللي حصل⁩ … ⁧بعدها⁩

Yāsmīn: Thank you. Look, the flight itself went well, but what happened next...
⁧في الأول كله تمام. وصلت المطار،⁩ : ⁧ياسمين⁩ ⁧ومشيت ورا الناس لحد مكان الشنط.⁩ ⁧وقفت أستنى، والشنط بتطلع واحدة ورا⁩ … ⁧التانية⁩

Yāsmīn: At first everything is fine. I got to the airport and followed people to the baggage pickup. I started waiting, and the bags came out one after the other...
Šarīf: And yours didn't go out, of course.
⁧استنى بس! كنت لسه واقفة،⁩ : ⁧ياسمين⁩ ⁧والناس مشيت كلها، وفجأة الحزام وقف.⁩ ⁧وأنا لوحدي!⁩

YāsmīnWait! I was still standing there, everyone was gone, and all of a sudden the tape stopped. And me alone!
Lūka: ya ḫabar! wi ʿamalti ēh?
Damn it! What did you do?
⁧كنت هعيط والله. بس رحت⁩ : ⁧ياسمين⁩ ⁧مكتب الشنط الضايعة، والموظفة قالتلي⁩ ⁧إن الشنطة لسه في القاهرة!⁩
Yasmīn: kunt haʿayyaṭ wallāhi. bass ruḥt maktab iš-šunaṭ iḍ-ḍayʿa, wi l- muwaẓẓafa ʾalitli inn iš-šanṭa lissa fi l- ʾAhira!
Yāsmīn: I was about to cry, I swear. But I went to the lost luggage office, and the clerk told me the suitcase was still in Cairo!
⁧وقالتلي أملا استمارة وأستنى⁩ : ⁧ياسمين⁩ ⁧تليفون. وأنا مش فاهمة نص الكلام⁩ ⁧بالإيطالي!⁩
Yasmīn: wi ʾalitli amla stimāra w- astanna tilifōn. wi ana miš fahma nuṣṣ il-kalām bi-l-iṭāli!
Yāsmīn: And he told me to fill out a form and wait for a phone call. And I didn't understand half of what he said in English!

Šarīf: However, the suitcase arrived yesterday, thank God.
⁧يا شريف! إنت كده بوظت القصة!⁩ : ⁧ياسمين⁩ ⁧كان لسه فيه حتة حلوة!⁩

blocks.text: No timing. In Egyptian the verb reported remains as it was: ʾalli inn iš-šanṭa lissa fi l-ʾAhira "He told me that the suitcase was still in Cairo" (Lett. It's still in the air. In Italian we make the concordance. The order reported. After ʾāl or ʾalli + person, the verb goes to the imperfect without bi-: ʾalli astana ʾalha tīgi bukra łle said to come tomorrow. You often hear the direct phrase: ʾalli . tiʾlaʾš"Don't worry," he said. The forms of ʾāl + there. ʾalli (to me) · ʾallak · ʾallik (a te m./f.) · ʾallu (to him) · ʾalha (to you) · ʾallina (to us) · ʾallukum (to you) · ʾalluhum (to them).
